sentences.text: Nichollssaura was an extinct genus of leptocleidid plesiosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous Boreal Sea of North America. This small marine reptile was estimated to reach 2.6 to 2.9 meters in length and 135 kilograms in body mass.
Parts of the holotype skeleton were accidentally lost when 100-ton electric shovel operators discovered the fossil.
The holotype specimen contained 165 gastroliths made of chert and quartzite, with the largest stone weighing an estimated 9.96 grams.
The type specimen was discovered in 1994 in an open-pit oil sands mine near Fort McMurray, Alberta, within the Wabiskaw member of the Clearwater Formation.
The holotype specimen preserves most of the skeleton, though it is missing the left forelimb and scapula, parts of the right hindlimb, and several ribs on the left side.
Researchers hypothesize that Nichollssaura swam westward to collect gastroliths from rocks that were 8 to 10 million years older than the animal itself.
The genus Nichollssaura was described by Druckenmiller and Russell in 2009 and is classified within the family Leptocleididae.
The genus was originally named Nichollsia in honor of curator Dr. Betsy Nicholls but had to be renamed because that name was already taken by a genus of isopods.
The type species N. borealis lived during the early Albian age in what is now Alberta, Canada. Nichollssaura lived between 113.2 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
